entry.title: Bitcoin Core v29.5 Released
entry.summary:
Bitcoin Core version 29.5 has been released and is available for download at [the official release page](https://bitcoincore.org/bin/bitcoin-core-29.5/). This update delivers a range of bug fixes, performance enhancements, and improved language translations. Users encountering issues are encouraged to report them through the [GitHub issue tracker](https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues), ensuring that feedback reaches the development team efficiently.
Upgrading to this version is straightforward. Users should first shut down any currently running instance of Bitcoin Core and allow it to close completely before proceeding with installation. On Windows, the standard installer can be used; on macOS, users should replace the `/Applications/Bitcoin-Qt` file; while on Linux, updating the `bitcoind` or `bitcoin-qt` binaries is sufficient. Direct upgrades from versions that have reached their end-of-life status are supported, though some migration time may be necessary for older data directories. Wallet compatibility remains broad, with legacy wallets continuing to be supported.
System compatibility is maintained with support for Linux Kernel 3.17 and above, macOS 13 and newer, as well as Windows 10 and later. While Bitcoin Core is expected to function on most Unix-like systems, such platforms are not tested as rigorously and use on unsupported systems is discouraged.
The new release introduces several notable technical changes. P2P improvements include the removal of a DNS seed and an assumption of v2transport for addresses received from seeds. Network-related updates align exception monitoring between poll() and select() backends, and enforce stricter timeout intervals for peers with paused sending. Utility enhancements involve storing positions in flatfiles using 64-bit integers, improving efficiency and scalability. Build processes now avoid the use of pipe2 on Darwin systems. Documentation has been updated to include BIP 433 (Pay to Anchor) and BIP 461 (Deterministic ECDSA signatures with low-R grinding), reflecting ongoing protocol evolution.
The development team acknowledges direct contributors—darosior, fanquake, Martin Zumsande, Sebastian Falbesoner, and sipa—and extends gratitude to everyone who contributed to translations and documentation. Further community engagement and announcements can be found at the [official mailing list](https://bitcoincore.org/en/list/announcements/join/).
